details.summary: Twilio Pay Connector — first-time setup & troubleshooting

div.p: This integration needs three things, in order. If any step is skipped the OAuth handshake in step 2 typically fails with UNSUPPORTED_ORIGIN.

ol.li:
Enable PCI Mode in Twilio (account-level, one-time)
Twilio Console → Develop → Voice → Settings → General → enable PCI Mode → Save.
⚠ Disables call recording on legs that execute <Pay> — a PCI-DSS requirement. Other recordings are unaffected. Cannot be reversed without Twilio support.

Install the Stripe Pay Connector in Twilio Marketplace
Twilio Console → Develop → Marketplace → search "Stripe Pay Connector" → Install → pick a unique name (e.g. HCStripe) → MODE = test for testing → click Connect with Stripe.
If "Connect with Stripe" fails with UNSUPPORTED_ORIGIN:
Confirm PCI Mode (step 1) is saved, then hard-refresh the Twilio Console (Cmd+Shift+R) or log out and back in.
Use Chrome in a clean incognito window.
In the same browser, log into Stripe first (dashboard.stripe.com), switch to Test mode, then open Twilio in a second tab and run the OAuth.
Disable ad blockers (uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger) for the Twilio tab.
Verify your Stripe account has business type set and email verified (Stripe Dashboard → Settings → Account details).
Last resort: open a Twilio support ticket with the Installed Connector SID from the configure page.

Configure the Odoo Stripe payment provider
Accounting → Configuration → Payment Providers → Stripe → set state to Test Mode → paste sk_test_… and pk_test_… from
Stripe Dashboard → Developers → API keys (Test mode).
Back here: enter the Pay Connector's unique name from step 2 in the field above and save. The "Stripe payment provider is active" banner should appear once step 3 is done.

div.p: Once setup is complete and verified with a test call, you may switch the payment.provider state from Test Mode to Enabled and the Pay Connector MODE in Twilio from test to live using your sk_live_… keys. Both sides must match (both test, or both live).
